title: Module quiz: Retrieval pipelines at design level

questions.stem: A legal-tech firm's assistant must answer from 3,000 agreements that are revised weekly, and every answer must cite its source. Clients may open only their own agreements. An engineer proposes fine-tuning a model on the agreements each month. Which design fits?

options.text: A model fine-tuned each month on the newest texts of the agreements, used with a short prompt
options.says: Ruled out because in the table the weights are weak when "Facts change, a source must be shown or a reader's access must be respected", which describes this firm.

options.text: The whole set of agreements placed in a single cached prompt that is shared by the clients
options.says: Ruled out because the prompt suits a corpus that is "small, shared by every request and edited rarely", and these agreements are revised weekly and read under access rules.

options.text: Section chunks in a permission-filtered index, replaced when their document changes
options.says: Frequent changes, citations and per-client access are retrieval's case, and a changed document must lose its old chunks.

options.text: A keyword index over each whole agreement, rebuilt from scratch each quarter by a batch job
options.says: Ruled out because "A re-index that runs less often than the documents change leaves old text in the index between runs", and a quarterly rebuild leaves it for months.

origin.section: Knowledge that changes: the prompt, retrieval or the weights

questions.stem: On a labelled set of 8 questions, a pipeline scores 4 ok, 1 generation, 2 retrieval and 1 unsupported. Where should the next week of work go?

options.text: The prompt alone, since one answer was wrong although its evidence was retrieved
options.says: Ruled out because "the pipeline has two retrieval failures and one generation failure".

options.text: The cut, the index and the freshness, since three problem cases lack evidence
options.says: The table sends retrieval outcomes to "The cut, the context, the index, the freshness".

options.text: Nowhere in particular, since five of the eight answers are right
options.says: Ruled out because "Counting only correct answers hides all three".

options.text: The unsupported case first, since a right answer needs no work at all
options.says: Ruled out because the table sends it to "Retrieval, because the answer rests on the model's memory or on luck".

questions.stem: A team re-indexes by adding the chunks of every changed document. Recall on its labelled questions stays high, yet users keep reporting outdated answers. What does the team's measurement miss?

options.text: Whether the keyword index outweighs the embedding index when the query holds a code
options.says: Ruled out because the weighting of codes decides ranking among current chunks, since "a question that names an identifier is the case where the keyword index is right", and it does not decide whether an old chunk is returned.

options.text: Whether the model follows the prompt when the evidence is present in its context
options.says: Ruled out because "the only thing that changed is what retrieval can return", so the old text is already in the evidence before the prompt is read.

options.text: Whether the labelled set holds enough questions about each topic of the support area
options.says: Ruled out because the problem is what the metric counts, as "an old chunk with the right id still counts as a hit", and more questions would count the same way.

options.text: Whether the passage that was returned still matches what its source says now
options.says: Recall by chunk id counts an old chunk with the right id as a hit, so staleness needs a check against the source.
